html:
The Korean state that ruled the peninsula from 918 to 1392. The English name Korea comes from Goryeo.

It was founded in 918 by the general Wang Geon, during the Later Three Kingdoms, when Silla was breaking apart. Silla's last king surrendered in 935, and Wang Geon reunited the peninsula the next year. He also took in many nobles from Balhae, the northern kingdom of Goguryeo's heirs, after its fall. Korean historians see this as the first true union of the peoples of the Three Kingdoms. The capital was Kaesong.

Goryeo was a golden age of Korean Buddhism and craft:

  • The state sponsored Buddhism, and the capital alone had about 70 temples in the 11th century.
  • Potters made the famous grey-green celadon ware.
  • Monks carved the whole Buddhist canon on more than 80,000 woodblocks, the Tripitaka Koreana.
  • In 1377 Goryeo printed the Jikji, the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type.
  • It held civil service exams on the Chinese model of the imperial examination.

Merchants came from China, Japan and as far as the Middle East.

Goryeo fought the Liao and paid tribute to the Jin. A military coup in 1170 left generals in control for a century. Then came the Mongols: from 1231 they invaded again and again, and Goryeo became a subject state whose kings married Mongol princesses. When Mongol power faded, the general Yi Seong-gye seized control and founded Joseon in 1392.
sum: The Korean state that ruled the peninsula from 918 to 1392. The English name Korea comes from Goryeo.
